html:
Sapa Inca, or emperor, of the Inca Empire from 1471 to 1493, and the son of Pachacuti. He did more than anyone to make the empire the largest state in the Americas.

He led his father's armies before he took the throne:

  • In the north he conquered the Chimú kingdom on the coast of Peru and pushed into what is now Ecuador, around Quito.
  • In the south he took much of Bolivia, northwest Argentina and central Chile, as far as the Maule River.
  • He also sent armies into the edge of the Amazon forest.

At home he organised the new lands with governors, censuses and the labour duty called the mit'a, and extended the road system. A legend says he sailed into the Pacific to distant islands; it may be no more than a story.

His son Huayna Capac followed him and ruled the empire at its height.
sum: Sapa Inca, or emperor, of the Inca Empire from 1471 to 1493, and the son of Pachacuti. He did more than anyone to make the empire the largest state in the Americas.
